IN RE: JOHN E MCNAMEE
PETITION FOR Review for Responsible Party
PERIOD(S) 1M10,9M10,10M10, 1M11,4M11,5M11,9M11
AND NOW, May 20, 2014, pursuant to the Fiscal Code, the Act of 1929, April 9, P.L. 343,
as amended, (72 P.S. § 1 et seq), the Board of Finance and Revenue of the Commonwealth of
Pennsylvania, based upon the reasons set forth herein, hereby ORDERS the following:
Jurisdiction
This petition comes before the Board of Finance and Revenue pursuant to Section 2704
of the Tax Reform Code of 1971, as amended, 72 P.S. § 9704.
Issue
Whether Petitioner has established that he was not a responsible party for the
deficiencies of the company during the period of assessment.
Statement of the Case
Petitioner, John E. McNamee, was assessed individually as secretary/treasurer, %
shareholder and a responsible party for the sales tax liabilities of Square Burrito, Inc., a
Pennsylvania S corporation operating a restaurant. The assessment consisted of sales taxes
totaling $ that were collected, but not remitted to the Commonwealth for the 1M10,
9M10, 10M10, 1M11, 4M11, 5M11 and 9M11. Petitioner was also assessed penalties and
interest.
The Board of Appeals denied the case noting that Petitioner was listed as
secretary/treasurer and % shareholder on the corporation’s 2009, 2010 and 2011
corporation returns, and Petitioner received RK-1 forms from the company showing his pass-
through income/loss from the company.
In the petition filed with the Board of Finance and Revenue, Petitioner requests
abatement of the assessment in its entirety. Petitioner explains that, in accordance with an

Arbitration Award, the company purchased his shares of the corporation on May 6, 2010.
Petitioner contends that he should not be held responsible for any liabilities incurred after that
date. Petitioner also claims he did not receive any RK-1 shareholder forms for 2009, 2010 and
2011, and he was not aware that the company was still entering his name on the tax
documents.
In support of the case, Petitioner submits the Arbitration Award dated January 25, 2011,
that acknowledges the corporation exercised its option to purchase his shares of the
corporation on May 6, 2010, for $ due to Petitioner’s violation of his shareholder
agreement. Petitioner was also ordered to repay the corporation for borrowed funds in the
amount of $ . Petitioner also submitted copies of the cancelled checks, dated May 6,
2010, issued to him from the corporation totaling $ .
Statement of the Law
All taxes collected by any person from purchasers in accordance with this article and all
taxes collected by any person from purchasers under color of this article which have not been
properly refunded by such person to the purchaser shall constitute a trust fund for the
Commonwealth, and such trust shall be enforceable against such person, his representatives
and any person (other than a purchaser to whom a refund has been made properly) receiving
any part of such fund without consideration, or knowing that the taxpayer is committing a
breach of trust: Provided, however, That any person receiving payment of a lawful obligation
of the taxpayer from such fund shall be presumed to have received the same in good faith and
without any knowledge of the breach of trust. Any person, other than a taxpayer, against
whom the department makes any claim under this section shall have the same right to petition
and appeal as is given taxpayers by any provisions of this part. 72 P.S. § 7225.
In George W. Brown III, as Individual and as President of Electrical Industries, Inc. v.
Commonwealth, 670 A.2d 1222 at 1225 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 1996), the Court determined that, for
the period when the bank took total control over the taxpayer and the officer had no control
over any financial operations, regardless of the fact that the officer remained on the premises
after the bank took control, the Officer was not liable for sales and withholding taxes. The
Court concluded that the taxpayer was not an active or controlling Officer of the corporation for
the period in which the bank held complete control over the financial operations of the
company. Conversely, the Court held that the taxpayer was liable for sales and withholding
taxes for the period in which he remained active and in control of the general management of
the business, including the financial operations.
In reaching this conclusion, the Court in Brown relied on the case of City of Philadelphia
v. B. Axe Company, 40 Pa. Commw. Ct. 257, 397 A.2d 51 (1979), wherein the Court
determined:
[A] corporation collecting taxes as an agent of a municipality
and failing to pay over such taxes to the municipality is a trustee ex
maleficio, and active and controlling corporate officers are
responsible for the performance of that trust duty by the

corporation. Where such persons fail to perform that duty, the
individuals are trustees ex maleficio as well as the corporation.
Id. at 261, 397 A.2d at 53.
The court in Axe also identified several factors that it considered important in
determining whether a corporate officer and shareholder was responsible for unpaid
withholding tax: physical presence on the premises at relevant times, ability to hire and fire
employees, review and signing tax documents, signing payroll checks, signing checks for
expenses, obtaining loans, consulting the company’s books, and acting as an administrator
and manager.
Conclusion
Petitioner’s request for relief is granted in part.
Upon review of the facts and evidence presented and in the exercise of our equitable
powers, this Board finds that Petitioner was not a responsible party for the 9M10, 10M10,
1M11, 4M11, 5M11 and 9M11 sales tax obligations of Square Burrito, Inc. After the
corporation purchased Petitioner’s shares on May 6, 2010, Petitioner was no longer a
shareholder and was not authorized to pay the company’s obligations. However, Petitioner
was liable for the trust fund obligations prior to the transfer.
ORDER
The Department of Revenue shall strike the responsible party assessment for the 9M10,
10M10, 1M11, 4M11, 5M11 and 9M11. Assessment number 020528-02 shall be reassessed
for only the 1M10 sales tax liability.
